sentences.text: Lourinhasaurus was a heavy-bodied herbivore with a long neck that reached about 17 meters in length.
This animal is estimated to have reached 15 to 18 meters in length and weighed around 5 metric tons, with a femur estimated to be 1.68 meters long.
The first seven dorsal vertebrae had relatively high and bifurcated neural spines, while posterior dorsal vertebrae featured prominent longitudinal keels in their centers.
Lourinhasaurus likely resembled Camarasaurus but had proportionally longer forelimbs.
The name Lourinhasaurus means "lizard from Lourinhã," even though the type specimen was not found in that municipality.
A second partial skeleton containing a tooth and one hundred gastroliths was found in 1983 near the city of Lourinhã.
The first fossil remains were discovered in June 1949 by American geologist Harold Weston Robbins near Alenquer.
In 1957, Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyszewski named the species Apatosaurus alenquerensis.
Pedro Dantas and colleagues proposed in 1998 that the taxon represented a distinct form from Apatosaurus and Camarasaurus, leading them to propose the new genus Lourinhasaurus.
The genus name Lourinhasaurus refers to the location of the second skeleton found.
Pedro Dantas and colleagues proposed the new genus name Lourinhasaurus in 1998 based on a specimen from Porto Dinheiro.
The Moinho do Carmo specimen was designated the lectotype for Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis in 2003.
A complete re-description and phylogenetic revision of Lourinhasaurus was published by Mocho and colleagues in 2014.
Lourinhasaurus was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur.
Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis is a member of the Eusauropoda and is classified in the class Saurischia.
The dinosaur was originally classified as a diplodocid.
In 2004, Upchurch determined that the species was more basal and a sister taxon to Neosauropoda.
A 2014 study by Mocho et al. suggested that Lourinhasaurus is a basal member of Macronaria and a type of Camarasauromorpha.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Lourinhasaurus is a basal Macronarian closely related to Camarasaurus, and the parent group for Lourinhasaurus is Camarasauridae.
Lourinhasaurus lived approximately 150 to 145 million years ago during the Late Jurassic, spanning the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages.
Lourinhasaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.

The classification of Lourinhasaurus has been controversial, with some specimens originally referred to it later reinterpreted as belonging to other genera like Dinheirosaurus, and the Porto Dinheiro specimen, initially used to define Lourinhasaurus, was later reinterpreted as a diplodocid named Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis.

In 1999, the second specimen was assigned its own genus name, Dinheirosaurus, and it is debated whether the second specimen should be classified as Lourinhasaurus or the separate genus Dinheirosaurus.
